summary: Try northern-style khanom jeen nam ngiao—fermented rice vermicelli in a tangy tomato and pork broth—as a contrasting noodle meal to khao soi. Sanpakoi Kanomjeen at Thongkam Market is a practical representative venue, with other curries available if someone in the group wants a milder alternative.
whyGo: Taste one of northern Thailand’s characteristic tomato-based noodle curries, commonly served with pork and local vegetables.
Sanpakoi Kanomjeen is a long-running local shop recognized by the MICHELIN Guide, with several curry choices and inexpensive street-food pricing.
The market setting and self-serve vegetables make it an easy, informal meal stop.
bestFor: Travelers who enjoy savory, sour and spicy noodle soups
A casual lunch or dinner near Chiang Mai’s San Pa Khoi and Ping River area
Groups who want different curries over rice noodles
skipIf: You avoid pork or meat stock and need a confirmed vegetarian, vegan or halal meal
You need guaranteed step-free access, accessible toilets or tightly controlled allergens
duration: Allow 30–60 minutes for a meal and possible queue; this is a planning estimate.
cost: Plan about THB 30–100 per person for a bowl and simple add-ons, based on current local reporting; budget extra for drinks. Estimate only: the MICHELIN Guide lists the venue in its lowest price tier, but no dated official menu was available.
hours: MICHELIN Guide lists Sanpakoi Kanomjeen open Monday–Saturday 11:00–23:00 and closed Sunday. Hours can change; confirm close to your visit.
bestTime: Go outside the busiest lunch and dinner periods for a more relaxed chance of finding a seat. Arrive before closing because individual dishes may sell out.
gettingThere: Sanpakoi Kanomjeen is at Thongkam Market, 11 Soi Thasatoi, on the east side of the Ping River. From the Old City, use a red songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hail to the market entrance, then walk through the market to the stall; allow roughly 10–20 minutes by vehicle depending on traffic (estimate). Check the map pin before setting off.
booking: Casual market dining; no advance booking is indicated. MICHELIN lists the shop as cash only, so bring small Thai baht notes. The guide lists phone +66 61 301 8000 for enquiries.
accessibility: The MICHELIN listing does not provide accessibility details. The venue is inside a market; step-free route, aisle width, seating and accessible toilet availability are unverified. Contact the venue before going if these are essential.
practicalTips: Order khanom jeen nam ngiao to try the northern tomato broth; the shop also serves other curries over rice noodles, or rice instead of noodles.
Expect pork in the signature broth; recipes often include pork stock and may include pork blood. Ask staff about the day’s ingredients and cross-contact rather than assuming a meat-free option.
The fresh vegetables and pickles help balance the rich, spicy broth. Add chilli gradually if heat-sensitive.
Carry cash and use the Thai venue name ขนมจีนสันป่าข่อย or the Thongkam Market address when asking for directions.
